text: Unchanged Python applications are checked against their models through the normal gate, with sampled evidence (#327, #328). `invariant verify` and `verify.Run` admit a Python manifest with nonempty `existing`, with or without components. One shared preflight rejects unsupported proof, exhaustive and attempted-step modes, missing invocations and mismatched drivers before any tool runs. One staged copy and one dependency image serve the whole run. Configured tests must actually run and pass. The driver's authenticated observations are checked against Init and Next with batched TLC at the ratified bounds, alongside every pin, ratification, design, witness, fairness, property and known-bug obligation. Receipts record actual executions, settings, inputs, dependencies, observations and independent outcomes under deterministic fingerprints, and mark each component row's origin as gate or supplied. They grant only sampled tested-against-the-model evidence, with no proof, exhaustive-state, every-step or every-size claim. Omitting components keeps a legacy receipt with no invented inventory, using ordinary unittest discovery and the manifest driver at default budgets. Exact JSON integers survive TLC encoding, and fractions fail explicitly.
